[olist]
[*] Valley of the Twelve
[*] The Etheros Path
[*] The Elysian Woods
[*] The Observatory

[/olist]

[*] The shadows handler is reduced by 30%
[*] The load memory handler is reduced by 20%
[*] The conflict between opening the large map while getting ambushed by enemies is now fixed.
[*] The conflict between the "Pause Menu", "Settings Menu", and "Map" is now resolved.
[*] The merchant's sell amount dialogue is redesigned to fit the rest of the merchant group UIs.
[*] Ambient Occlusion removed from the largest maps in the game.
[/list]

notes.title: Update 0.8.19
notes.content:
Greetings, Update 0.8.19 is a combat special update and brings an additional combat mechanic. Introducing:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/80c0f4bf65a237db813205cde14b5bab08c24e50.png[/img]
Each character in your party will have an Anima gauge that charges during combat, the moment it reaches 100% you will be able to execute an Anima Latent Skill. These supercharged attacks inflict heavy damage and will surely help you in your battles.

[previewyoutube=JV4XZKiUbz8;full][/previewyoutube]
[i][b]Video Subject: Fiona/Mirabelle/Adriel's Anima Latent Skill[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/95977fff3cbb6c3ea4b8514a48b8b0e79d09cd85.png[/img]
[list]
[*] [b]How does the Anima Gauge charge?[/b]
[*] The Anima gauge charges when you inflict or receive damage. The Latent Anima Skill doesn't require any MP or consumable to be used.
[*] [b]Is the Anima Latent Skill damage physical or magical?[/b]
[*] The Anima Latent Skill combines both your magical and physical stats and inflicts damage on both your enemies' physical and magical defense plus a multiplier.
[*] [b]Is there a way to charge the Anima gauge quickly?[/b]
[*] There are two ways to get a bonus charge :

[list]
[*][b]A:[/b] By switching to "Aggressive Mode" the Anima Gauge will charge faster, the UI will show you that when you Switch/Adapt Combat Mode. (Careful though, when you switch to "Defensive Mode" the Anima charges at a slower rate).
[*][b]B:[/b] When you use a skill that inflicts critical damage on your enemies.
[/list]
[*] [b]Does the Anima gauge reset after the combat ends?[/b]
[*] No! The bar keeps its current percentage after the battle ends, you flee, or even if the character dies. You can use this to your advantage. For example, you can charge the Anima gauge for all your attack party before getting into a boss fight.
[*] [b]How can I keep track of my Anima gauge during and outside a battle?[/b]
[*] During a battle you will see a new UI part added to the left, this UI includes the progress bar, the percentage, and it will change and start pulsing when it's filled while showing the key combinations to execute. While exploring on the other hand you can open the camp menu and you will notice the additional element added to each character (The same line as strength/weakness.)
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/da8c8ffc054b45f5b43c8e0bdbbdd1a9be74734a.png[/img]
In addition to the highlight of this update, there were also a few small updates that correct certain issues as the following:

[list]
[b][*]All the Anime style artwork of the boss fights intros' UI has been optimized.
[*]NPC Dialogue and UI prompt animated.
[*]Save/Load UI issue with the highlights is fixed.
[*]Cassandra's stun animation is reworked.
[*]SFX ambient radius is enlarged during combat.[/b]
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/5a5906d0130c04131d78d03252a3b32a29fe114b.png[/img]
I hope that this special update brings you an enjoyable combat system and helps you pair both the Adapt Combat Mode, MP economy, and now the Anima Latent Skill charging.

[b][h3]Thank you again for your continued support for this world, characters, and story.[/h3][/b]

[i]Kind Regards,
Zine. E. Falouti[/i]

notes.title: Alder Forge Devlog #4
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/4166b0f3ba4e610f5c02d4b7c98b97c04d5d7a32.png[/img]
After the weapons design and the first round of primary gameplay testing, the next step in the production process is Scoring the Music, the music in the Alder Forge is not only an ornament to fill the space of that world, but a part of the story, each track composed is significantly related to either a character, an organization, a Royal House or just the area you are in, and of course, that includes the enemies you will face, each group has a piece of signature music related to them.
 
And without further ado, let us start with the anatomy of the Alder Forge main theme, to give you an idea of the structure and groups of instruments used to score the subject track.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/3754bfc2e4f6a3099ad073bf13d109c9485f4d25.png[/img]
[previewyoutube=N0hp6UFhk2Q;full][/previewyoutube]
[i][b]Video Subject: Anatomy of the Alder Forge Main Theme[/b][/i]

As you can see the most dominant instruments are the strings, I usually combine multiple articulations at once, usually, the Spiccato and Legato/Staccato, which helps me produce a more nuanced melody, the strings are also involved but not always in the Chord Progression.

Before I start composing I always split my DAW into multiple chambers as the following, then I begin afterward with either sketching a Chord Progression, a Melody, or both at the same time.

Here are the multiple split sections used to score the music for the Alder Forge:
[list]
[*] The Strings Section
[*] The Brass/Woodwinds Section
[*] The Keys Section
[*] The Percussion Section
[*] The Choir Section
[*] The Electronic Section
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/14b01a4bc2ca690a4cd322b2f8e0ff96009d1f1a.png[/img]
[i][b]Image Subject: Most dominant instruments used in the Alder Forge music[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/56270b6bea8d0a3487db71b16a71247afc2635fa.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/c3441eb6ddde5caa51e851f599aed95c58ac54f8.png[/img]
[i][b]Image Subject: Hardware & Software used to record and score the Alder Forge music[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/a9c9c245e35261b3088fcca79f9d366eff44d14e.png[/img]

The Gaming Community are no stranger to Leitmotifs, so there is no necessity in defining the term or explaining it, and like many other worlds, the Alder Forge also has established and defined its Leitmotifs as the following:

[list]
[*] The Alder Forge:[b] Established[/b]
[*] The Equilibrium:[b] Established[/b]
[*] The Magna Lumen:[b] Established[/b]
[*] The Atlas Court:[b] Established[/b]
[*] The Netherwaves:[b] Planned for Chapter 2[/b]
[*] De Roy Family:[b] Established[/b]
[*] Sieg Vulpes Family:[b] Planned for Chapter 2[/b]
[*] Val Fiery Family:[b] Planned for Chapter 3[/b]
[*] Er Aquila Family:[b] Planned for Chapter 4[/b]
[/list]

Here are 3 Leitmotifs melody/chord progressions that are recurrent, especially in Chapter 1, played with the Grand Piano:

[previewyoutube=Oi58QbbZgLU;full][/previewyoutube]
[i][b]Video Subject: 3 Leitmotifs played with the Grand Piano[/b][/i]

[h3][b]PS: Please note that I'm not trying to overstep your boundaries, I'm well aware that the only ones who can establish, nominate and name the Leitmotifs are the Alder Forge Community, I'm only establishing the themes, whatever you call a Leitmotif or not shall be respected.[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/95a4a34943ce1cd90c23ab480b4bf371e9c499a5.png[/img]

Scoring the music for the Alder Forge requires that I finish the Environment Design, Enemies, and Cinematic for the subject area, which helps me establish the theme or the motion that I need to compose to accompany the player's experience while exploring or fighting in that portion of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/54f59a96b3a2e03ba74139db32d73182ad17bd92.png[/img]
[i][b]Image Subject: Official artwork for the upcoming Soundtrack DLC[/b][/i]

Thank you again for your support and appreciation for the last 3 Devlogs, in the remaining Devlog we will dive into the Lighting, Optimization, and a bonus (Real-time Cinematic).

[b][h3]Before the upcoming Devlog, the Early Access Phase 1 Release Date will also be announced.[/h3][/b]

Kind Regards,
Zine E.Falouti

notes.title: Alder Forge Devlog #3
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/4166b0f3ba4e610f5c02d4b7c98b97c04d5d7a32.png[/img]

Designing the weapons in the Alder Forge is not a one-stop process that comes after the character design but an ongoing active one, the reason for that is populating the weapons throughout the world and the Players' ability to acquire them, and each weapon should not only differ by stats and perhaps skills but also by the design itself, and without further ado let us begin with the first step of the weapons design process.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/10a6386b81ce4b85cde2df5478aaa86d96284caf.png[/img]
[i][b]Image subject: Design sheet of the Silver Blades.[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/3fc1218e249013128ba5029b91d89a73aa8e8277.png[/img]
Some weapons may not require this process if they are solely nonrealistic,  but the majority are influenced by real-life historical weapons (Swords, axes, etc ..) or contemporary weapons (Guns, muskets, canons, etc...).
The mood board research always takes me to gather imagery of museums displays, blacksmiths, or historical documentaries to gather as much information as I can, not only to be faithful to the historical design but at least to have a base that respects the function and name of the said weapon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/0d3428489c6373a9fe697ca7f82b1c4c54cd44d2.png[/img]
[i][b]Image subject: Orvysian Cinquedea Mood Board.[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/25a6eeac6cd7f9b9ddffbf3fffc46054ae8b5be6.png[/img]
The production pipeline for all the weapons is the same as the prop design you saw in Devlog #1 (Environment Design), but with the addition of a pre-process that requires sketching the base shapes, 3d modeling on top of the produced shapes, then starting with the open 3d/sculpting workshop as showcased in the example below.

[previewyoutube=r1gHkHIGAX8;full][/previewyoutube]
[i][b]Video subject: Orvysian Cinquedea and the Silver Blade Design Showcase[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/f1f8d73c208c9e7bcf5fe5b663c38713a9ae8256.png[/img]
All the weapons categories might have the same production pipeline but they completely differ in art direction and the way they are basically produced. In the Alder Forge, the categories are split into 4 plus other categories that are produced solely for certain mobs, bosses, or important NPCs as showcased below. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/6cf3b3bd13c7c8cbfb996d87d364949d055979ee.png[/img]
[i][b]Image subject: Main Characters/Party Weapon Categories[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/13a2aab48ead1da1a8af85f0349d439c02028afc.png[/img]
[i][b]Image subject: Mob, Bosses & NPCs Categories[/b][/i]

[previewyoutube=MMFByyfpUcU;full][/previewyoutube]
[i][b]Video subject: Bows, Axes and Staves Design Showcase[/b][/i]

[previewyoutube=fMymQMTZgZw;full][/previewyoutube]
[i][b]Video subject: Guns and Rifles Design Showcase[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/66713cd380bb7b68d0259645f40d16d6af44466e.png[/img]
[b]Air Stormers Definition in the game: [/b]The Air Stormers are vessels that run on Anima without an engine, but they use a volatile reaction that happens within the core of each vessel which makes them different than Air Ships in the world of the Alder Forge, but also makes them more powerful and produced solely for warfare reasons, unlike the Airships in the game which are produced for slow travel, here is an example of the design and in Engine assembly of one of the Equilibrium Air Stormers [b]"The Lambrador"[/b].

[previewyoutube=h-4zNPYMqEM;full][/previewyoutube]
[i][b]Video subject: Air Stormer Design and In Engine Assembly[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/d5ea358d740f5775f0c4ed24410d2ed78d98cba9.jpg[/img]
[i][b]Image subject: Side by side artwork of both the Silver Blades and the Sixth Gauntlet[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/95a4a34943ce1cd90c23ab480b4bf371e9c499a5.png[/img]
The weapons design process was established at the beginning of the Alder Forge production and is symmetrically produced alongside the combat design, skill design but also the progression of the story, each map completed requires me to design the weapons related to the culture of that area, habits, and history.

And similar to the Character Design, the Weapons Design is also heavily influenced by the story and characters that will wield or operate such weapons.

In the upcoming Devlogs we will dive into each of the remaining subjects:
[list]
[*] Music and Scoring
[*] Lighting, Shading & Optimization
[/list]

Thank you for your continued support and appreciation for the latest devlogs and I will continue showcasing behind the curtain details of the development of this world and story.

Kind Regards,
Zine. E. Falouti

notes.title: Alder Forge Devlog #2
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/4166b0f3ba4e610f5c02d4b7c98b97c04d5d7a32.png[/img]
After the environment design the second most time consuming process is of course the character design, you will find that this process is somehow similar in matter of pre production but completely changes the moment the character is skinned/rigged and in Game ready.

In my production process I have split the importance and type of all the characters into three groups:
[list]
[*]1- Important characters, Main Cast and Bosses
[*]2- Mob and Mini Bosses
[*]3- NPCs, pets and other creatures.
[/list]

And without further ado let us begin with two example characters and their workflow from Group 1.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/21dbcc79404fa45e7555fdd995f9c6f4e97847c7.png[/img]
[i][b][h3]Character In Game Ready Preview: Louise[/h3][/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/43c43fed3956a2f4274230902a7dbbacb6a00b8a.png[/img]

[previewyoutube=K4XnW40oaaI;full][/previewyoutube]
[b][i][h3]Video Subject: Louise Character Pieces and Design Workflow[/h3][/i][/b]

As you can see the process requires to individually design and adapt each garment piece, jewelry and even small accessories (Like Earrings, rings, family emblems or affiliation), the latter will help you see and 
understand the characters you will meet and their affiliation, but also give each one of them a function, please note that all these element choices are made by the story of each character and their future in that world.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/595b2221026f0d825dd6355ba29a66562ebdff9c.png[/img]
[i][b][h3]Character In Game Ready Preview: Adriel[/h3][/b][/i]
[previewyoutube=eioAY731mSc;full][/previewyoutube]
[b][i][h3]Video Subject: Adriel Character Pieces and Design Workflow[/h3][/i][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/11dedb62f94b104b639071a497cb1d00e931f9ad.png[/img]

Robotic characters are characters that have no organic element at all, and are designed by assembling multiple pieces that are generally bipedal or close to a human form, like the [b]HXP Interceptors [/b] for example, these characters never get into the sculpting chamber, but instead they go through the "Hard Surface Modeling Chamber", here is an example of an HXP Interceptor you are familiar with.

[previewyoutube=UZMFbifkjCc;full][/previewyoutube]
[b][i][h3]Video Subject: Interceptor Hard Surface Modeling[/h3][/i][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/6fe3148d04449355d178b3b301311068a7f770fb.png[/img]
For certain mob, monsters and even other creatures that serve a storyline purpose an organic character workflow is mandatory and each body part is produced via the sculpting chamber, retopology/baking and finally painting, here is an example of a mob full production.

[previewyoutube=6CjVO1DBk1Q;full][/previewyoutube]
[previewyoutube=pWP2l6NQegc;full][/previewyoutube]
[b][i][h3]Videos Subject: Character Organic Workflow example[/h3][/i][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/061543abee9c254b97079833d984ff7a454ab098.png[/img]
Control Rigs are in-Engine scripting tool that helps code the motions and control elements to either modify existing animations or even make new ones, usually used for cinematic purposes, but can also be used for in game dynamic motions, here is an example video that showcase this exact workflow.

[previewyoutube=tFYts_klz5o;full][/previewyoutube]
[b][i][h3]Video Subject: Control Rig Scripting and Use Case[/h3][/i][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/289f606db927a65caf5b71ac7ff85653ce11b42e.png[/img]
[i][b][h3]Adriel and Louise side by side artwork[/h3][/b][/i]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/95a4a34943ce1cd90c23ab480b4bf371e9c499a5.png[/img]
The Character Design process in the Alder Forge always come after the Environment Design of each area, to either populate, enrich story elements or cinematic, but most importantly, it is the main funnel that supply the combat system of the game.

In the upcoming Devlogs we will dive in each of the remaining subjects:
[list]
[*] Weapons Design
[*] Lighting & Shading
[*] Scoring & Music Composition
[*] Optimization
[/list]


I humbly thank you for reading this Devlog and your continued interest in the world of the Alder Forge.

Kind Regards,
Zine. E.Falouti

notes.title: Alder Forge Devlog #1
notes.content:
Greetings,

   As per the tradition for each one of my games, it is time to start with the Devlogs, each devlog that will be published will be related to the multiple disciplines and work I did while building the Alder Forge, so you could have an open curtain dev view of the game and see how each element was created, and without further ado, let us begin with Devlog #1 (Environment Design).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/4166b0f3ba4e610f5c02d4b7c98b97c04d5d7a32.png[/img]

     Environment design is the most time consuming process in all of the Game production supply chain, taking over 65% of the total time and that doesn't even include scripting or either character design, for the simple reason that I had to handcraft, sculpt and model each architectural, prop or structural asset, but the first thing I do before starting each level, area, city, village or stronghold is building Mood Boards and references before starting on the first most dominant item of all, (The Trims).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/62c78256ceae7799c2c6d4e03099f438a407a36a.png[/img]

   Trims & PBRs are the materials and modular textures that dominate the architectural skeleton of each map, thus I always prefer to hand sculpt both of these elements for the simple reason to build a unique and original personality for the Alder Forge game as showcased in the video below:

[previewyoutube=en2xDTQ6lo4;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3][b]Video Subject:[/b] Trim Sheets Design[/h3]

[previewyoutube=zadmFA72NsM;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3][b]Video Subject:[/b] Wooden Roof PBR Full Design Process (Speed x5)[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/124f941fe071c2e8d0971a329f52b2afc8ecd41a.png[/img]

[h3]How the PBR shown in the video is built in the example of the PAX Residence (Atlas Court)[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/18ad43c19ea8cfa9751cb41f217e21fab4ef8551.png[/img]

    Unlike the Architectural Modular Pieces, the props are required in my design process to go individually through the following pipeline.

[list]
[*]Sketching the shapes (2D)
[*]3D Modeling & Base Blocking
[*]Sculpting, Baking & Retopology
[*]Texture painting & Material assembly
[/list]

     For every prop with a base element of steel, I always paint the Black PBR first, that helps me highlight the rough edges and scratches before adding a layer and painting the final PBR as showcased in the video below:

[previewyoutube=FMQ2Tz34XOk;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3][b]Video Subject:[/b] Prop Example and Structure[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/b765593a5b90102af7355da340e11b411a8bbcf4.png[/img]

    Both The Trim and PBR process final purpose is to design and build the architectural pieces, a group of 3D elements each designed with capability in mind to be composed together and build the structure of the world, here is an example of all the Modular assets that were designed to build the Voxenhold Fortress.

    Few of the Single Modular Assets are then grouped into prefabs, to compose other structures, like the towers in Voxenhold or the Bridge, this grouping helps me gain time and optimization before starting the Level Design process.

[previewyoutube=G5x4sB527N0;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3][b]Video Subject:[/b] Voxenhold Ground & Bridge Modular Assets[/h3]

    Yet certain architectural assets don't follow the standard pipeline and require to be detail sculpted and handcrafted due to either their importance in the story, gameplay or just their related view to the Player Camera position, (The Arch and the Lower Walls in Voxenhold are an example) here is a showcase of the Arch design & the Barricade Pieces.

[previewyoutube=qDEBgZC1F9I;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3][b]Video Subject:[/b] Arch & Barricade Design Showcase[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/b78d0e693914c242c374e97b7ce4a9b2842a5d44.png[/img]

[h3]Baked Rendered Shot of Voxenhold[/h3]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40116724/95a4a34943ce1cd90c23ab480b4bf371e9c499a5.png[/img]

  Each element in the Alder Forge game's environment is handcrafted through the process explained previously, and each element is grouped by a degree of position and importance to be classified in each pipeline. You may ask about the Lighting & Shading, and you are right to do so, because of its importance in the environment design process, but that discipline alone is so complicated and big that it deserves a Devlog of its own which I will publish before the Early Access starting point.

    In the upcoming Devlogs we will dive in each of the following subjects:
    [list]
[*]Character Design
[*]Weapons Design
[*]Lighting & Shading
[*]Scoring & Music Composition
[*]Optimization
[/list]

    [i]Thank you for reading this Devlog and your interest in the world of the Alder Forge.[/i]

Kind Regards,
Zine. E.Falouti
